data.narrative:
Terrestrial Energy operates in the nuclear energy sector as a public company, having raised $280M to date. The valuation universe comprises 11 sector peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private entities, with top private comparables including Oklo, X-Energy, Helion, Valar Atomics, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. The nuclear energy sector contains only 6 same-sector peers total. When filtered by stage alignment and valuation tier, the peer set yields fewer than 3 datapoints—the minimum threshold required for statistical reliability. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias and obscure the specific capital intensity and commercialization dynamics of nuclear technology development.

Without triangulation support from comparable valuation multiples, this analysis cannot produce a defensible valuation range. A credible conclusion would require either: (1) expansion of the comparable set through adjacent energy-tech subsectors, (2) application of discounted cash flow or sum-of-the-parts methods using Terrestrial Energy's specific project economics, or (3) direct precedent transaction analysis within nuclear. The thinness of the nuclear peer universe—particularly at Terrestrial Energy's stage and scale—remains the binding constraint on market-based valuation approaches.
